messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: smart-routing-service elevated error rate 500s -> detected region fallback flood. Auto-create incident. https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/2299999999 :rotating_light:
Dmitri: I’m seeing a surge of requests being routed to eu-west-2-beta-quantized. Error rate 502/504 from runtime. Possible variant mismatch + retry amplification. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: Pager: Dmitri is oncall for infra. Handoff window 02:00-10:00 UTC. Escalation sent to SRE.
Carla: Observed client-side retries from some SDK versions (v1.12) with aggressive backoff=0.5s, max_attempts=6. When runtime fails, smart-router falls back to regional variant, which causes double traffic.
Ben: Logs show fallback_count spiking from 3 -> 1200 in 10m and upstream capacity auto-scaled but CPU/KV cache thrashing. Snippet from router logs:
```
[2299999999] route_request: model=redwood-base, variant=stable -> mismatch -> fallback_to=eu-west-2-beta-quantized
[2299999999] fallback_count=1234, retry_from_client=4
[2299999999] kv_cache_miss=98%, token_latency_ms=340
```
Dmitri: Root cause hypothesis: routing policy allowed variant_family mapping that returned a quantized beta variant for customers who pinned to `stable`, and the variant is incompatible with current runtime kernel selection -> transient failures -> clients retry -> router sends them to alternate region/variant -> thundering herd.
Carla: Confirmed: a recent policy change to allow "approximate_variant_match: true" for better cost routing was rolled out 6 hours ago. Policy log:
```
policy_id: p-78fa
approximate_variant_match: true
fallback_regions: [eu-west-2, us-west-1]
priority: cost_then_latency
```
Alice: That flag should never have been enabled for pinned enterprise tenants. It caused mismatch for ~14 enterprise customers who had strict variant constraints.
Kari (Customer Success): I opened a ticket with the largest affected customer (AcmeBooks), their app saw 8x latency and 30% error tail. They asked if we could route back to their pinned variant ASAP.
Ben: Mitigation plan: 1) Disable approximate_variant_match globally for 10m as an immediate stopgap. 2) Apply strict_variant_match for pinned customers. 3) Add temporary edge throttles to reduce retry blast (token-bucket 50r/s per customer). 4) Roll back policy change in canary.
Dmitri: Executing mitigation step 1 now -> `curl -X POST https://admin-api/policies/p-78fa/disable` -> response 200. Noting propagation to edge within ~60s.
Carla: Pushing strict config for tenant pins: `PUT /tenants/acme/policy {"strict_variant_match": true}` -> applied.
Ben: Deploying temporary throttle rules at edge: `edgectl apply throttle --tenant acmebooks --rate 50/s --burst 100` -> applied.
incidents-bot: SYSTEM: policy change rolled back for p-78fa by Dmitri at 2299999999. Propagation status: 3/5 control planes, 2/5 pending.
Dmitri: Control plane propagation done 229999 (3 min). Runtime nodes still draining KV thrash, but tail error rates dropped from 18% -> 4% in 5m.
Alice: Can we tweak client retry guidance? We should issue a temporary SDK patch to backoff multiplier -> 2x and max_attempts 3.
Carla: Filed SDK advisory: https://redwood.internal/devex/alerts/2299999999-sdktweak. Short-lived release published to CDN, but not everyone will pick it up.
Kari (Customer Success): I told AcmeBooks support team we're applying mitigations and will follow up with a postmortem. They acknowledged.
Ben: Still seeing some hotspots: us-west-1 fallback traffic remains elevated. We're routing that to warm standby pool to avoid further failovers.
Dmitri: On-call handover in 30m to Ben. Ben will monitor scaling and rollback if needed.
oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: Dmitri -> Ben at 2300000000.
Ben: Taking over. Current action items: watch error rate, ensure throttle holds, verify canary rollback, prepare rollback script for policy change.
Alice: Post-incident immediate actions: 1) Revert approximate_variant_match in config-store (done). 2) Add guardrail to disallow enabling it for pinned_tenants. 3) Add analytic alert for fallback amplification ratio > 2.
Carla: Also adding a safety in smart-router: if fallback_count spikes and client_retry_rate > 20%, temporarily disable automated fallback for that tenant for 60s. Will submit PR.
Ben: Customer impact summary so far (quick): ~14 tenants affected, worst-case latency x8, error rate spike up to 30% short window. No data loss. Billing effect: slight overage due to retries; finance notified.
Kari (Customer Success): I'm drafting a support message for affected customers: simple clear steps and ETA for postmortem.
Dmitri: Status update at +20m: error rate stabilized to baseline (1.2%). KV cache hit improved to 72%. Still watching.
Ben: Closing the immediate incident once we confirm 30m stable. Will open a follow-up ticket for policy auditing and SDK guidance.
Alice: Assign follow-ups: Policy audit -> Alice, Router guardrail PR -> Carla, SDK advisory enforcement -> DevEx, Customer comms -> Kari.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: incident 2299999999 moved to monitoring at 2300000200.
Dmitri: Thanks all. We'll run a blameless postmortem. Key takeaway: fallback heuristics need circuit-breakers for retry amplification. :white_check_mark:
